questions.prompt: How does the C# TaskItem in the translation guide reproduce the Java Task value object? Explain what record and get-only properties each provide, what the constructor checks for id and version, what the Text helper enforces on title and description, how Edit produces a change, and how version overflow is handled.

keyPoints.text: A record gives value equality; get-only properties give immutability.
keyPoints.quote: A `record` gives you value equality, and get-only properties give you immutability.

keyPoints.text: The constructor rejects a non-positive id or version.
Text trims the value and rejects lengths outside the bounds or any control characters.
Edit mirrors Java's Task.edit: a new value with the next version, with validation re-run.
keyPoints.quote: new value, next version, validation re-run

keyPoints.text: checked turns version overflow into an exception, like Java's nextVersion.
keyPoints.quote: `checked` turns version overflow into an exception

keyPoints.text: In Java, nextVersion throws once the version reaches Integer.MAX_VALUE.

questions.prompt: What two Java-to-C# traps does the translation guide warn about when porting Task? Explain what Java's compact constructor does in TaskSnapshot and why a positional C# record cannot copy it, what the example does instead, what a with-expression would bypass, and how the example stops with from being used so edits must go through Edit.

keyPoints.text: C# has no compact constructor.
Java's TaskSnapshot validates in a compact constructor block.
A positional record cannot validate its parameters in a constructor body, so the example uses an explicit constructor.
keyPoints.quote: cannot validate its parameters in a constructor body, so this example uses an explicit constructor.

keyPoints.text: A with-expression copies the object and sets the property directly: no validation runs and Version is not bumped.
keyPoints.quote: copies the object and sets the property directly, so no validation runs and `Version` is not bumped.

keyPoints.text: So the properties have no init accessor, which means with cannot set them.
keyPoints.quote: That is why the properties have no `init` accessor (so `with` cannot set them)

keyPoints.text: Edits go through Edit, just as Java callers must use edit or withCompletion.
keyPoints.quote: just as Java callers must use `edit`/`withCompletion`.

questions.prompt: How does the translation guide port the Java version check and file-baseline comparison to EF Core and SQL? Explain how the row's version is marked, what the service does before and during the save, what SQL predicate results and how zero affected rows is surfaced and mapped over HTTP, how the same check looks as one SQL statement, when the new version may be reported, and what the exercise's two tests assert.

keyPoints.text: The row's Version carries [ConcurrencyCheck] (or a [Timestamp] RowVersion).
The service compares the loaded row's version with the expected one and throws a stale-edit error on mismatch.
EF turns the attribute into a WHERE Version = @expected predicate, the same check the Java course simulates with the file baseline.
keyPoints.quote: EF Core turns `[ConcurrencyCheck]` into the `WHERE Version = @expected` predicate

keyPoints.text: Zero affected rows becomes DbUpdateConcurrencyException, mapped to 409.
keyPoints.quote: zero affected rows becomes the exception you map to 409.

keyPoints.text: As one SQL statement: update where id and expected version match; 1 row means accepted, 0 means a stale edit.
Commit before report survives: return the new version only after SaveChangesAsync has returned.
keyPoints.quote: return the new version only after `SaveChangesAsync` (the commit) has returned.

keyPoints.text: Exercise: two contexts load task 1, both save a title change, and the second must throw DbUpdateConcurrencyException.
The HTTP version uses If-Match: "1" and answers 428 when the header is missing.
keyPoints.quote: a 428 when the header is missing.
